records.title: Neural Machine Translation between Low-Resource Languages with Synthetic Pivoting
records.reason: Tried the DOI landing page; it did not resolve to an accessible primary paper. The input metadata/abstract describe low-resource machine translation using synthetic pivoting, but the body and evaluation cannot be checked. The topic is translation quality rather than inference efficiency, and unavailable primary text requires a reasoned borderline.

records.title: A General and Efficient Training for Transformer via Token Expansion
records.reason: Token Expansion introduces a transformer training strategy that expands token representations to improve training efficiency and convergence, evaluating language-model quality and training costs. It does not demonstrate reduced deployment memory/latency or serving cost. The linked pruning paper is only a training-efficiency adjacency.

records.title: Calabash: Accelerating Attention Using a Systolic Array Chain on FPGAs
records.reason: Tried the DOI/IEEE publisher record and search for an author full-text copy; no accessible primary paper body was obtained. Calabash is described bibliographically as an FPGA systolic-array chain for attention acceleration, but its method, evaluation and limitations remain unverified. Record borderline until the actual publisher record or author copy is available.

records.title: A Self-Attention Network for Deep JSCCM: The Design and FPGA Implementation
records.reason: Tried the IEEE publisher record; the full paper body was not accessible. The title indicates FPGA implementation of self-attention for deep joint source-channel coding, an application-specific communications model rather than LLM serving; without full text, its relation to the linked FPGA transformer work is uncertain. Final borderline.

records.title: Improving Non-autoregressive Generation with Mixup Training
records.reason: Mixup training creates synthetic examples for non-autoregressive generation and evaluates translation quality versus NAR baselines. It aims to improve model quality, not reduce inference steps or hardware cost; no direct efficiency gain is established. Its training method is adjacent to the linked iterative-refinement NAR lineage, so retain as borderline.
